attempts.summary: Configured a DHCP relay chain so node3 obtains its address from the DHCP service on node2, despite node2 and node3 sitting on different L2 segments off node1. Assigned node1's eth1 (192.168.21.1/24, facing node2) and eth2 (192.168.22.1/24, facing node3) as gateways with IP forwarding enabled; gave node2 a static address (192.168.21.10/24) on its segment-facing NIC; installed and configured Kea DHCP4 on node2 with a relayed subnet declaration for 192.168.22.0/24 (giaddr 192.168.22.1, pool .100-.200, routers 192.168.22.1); installed and configured isc-dhcp-relay (dhcrelay) on node1 listening on eth1+eth2 and forwarding to node2's 192.168.21.10. Verified node3 obtained 192.168.22.100 via the relay and confirmed the lease recorded on node2. All configuration was made persistent (interfaces.d static stanzas, sysctl.d forwarding, systemd-enabled kea-dhcp4 and isc-dhcp-relay services). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and health baselines on all three nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via native reboot commands, polled each until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified post-restart recovery — node1's static addressing/forwarding/dhcrelay all came back automatically, node2's kea-dhcp4 service and prior lease data survived, and node3 automatically re-acquired its DHCP-relayed address (192.168.22.100) from node2 with no manual intervention after its reboot.
